title: Biomonitoring of airborne metals using tree leaves: Protocol for biomonitor selection and spatial trend
author: Hajizadeh, Mokhtari, et al.

steps.title: Wash leaf samples
steps.instruction: Weigh 50 g of fresh leaves from each selected biomonitor, wash consecutively with tap water, then rinse three times with deionized water to remove impurities.

steps.title: Dry and grind leaves
steps.instruction: Dry the cleaned leaves in an oven at 80 °C for 72 h, then grind them to a fine powder.

steps.title: Acid digestion of sample
steps.instruction: Place 1 g of the dried powdered sample into a Teflon high‑pressure digestion vial (Applied Plastics Technology, Inc., Bristol, USA), add a acid mixture of HNO₃ 70 %, HCl 70 % and HF 40 % in a 9:3:1 ratio, warm at 50 °C for 2 h, then mineralize at 170 °C for 4 h.

steps.title: Post‑digestion treatment
steps.instruction: After cooling, add 2 mL of 30 % H₂O₂ and 3 mL of concentrated HNO₃ to the digested sample, dilute the solution to a final volume of 50 mL with Milli‑Q water, and filter through a 0.45 µm micro‑porous membrane into a PET bottle.

steps.title: Prepare blank digest
steps.instruction: Process a blank digest solution in parallel using the same reagents, volumes, temperatures, and times as the sample digestion steps.

steps.title: ICP‑AES analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the filtered extracts for Fe, Cd, Cu, Ni, Pb, Zn, Na (metals) and As (metalloid) using inductively coupled plasma‑atomic emission spectrometry (ICP‑AES, Model Arcous, Germany) according to USEPA Method 200.7.
